- [LADP.10.2.2] **Avoiding own-action feedback.** A rule that fires
  `call light.turn_on entity_id: ...` will see the resulting state
  change arrive as a fact, and usually should not react to it.
  Telling that fact apart from a genuine external change means
  comparing its `context_id` against the context the rule's own call
  produced.

  **DS cannot supply the second value.** A rule may compare
  `l.context_id` against anything it can name, but nothing in the
  language records the context id an outgoing `call` caused. That
  exists only if the adapter reports it back, which [LADP.10.2.1]
  treats as optional. So in v1 the pattern is open only to
  integrations whose adapter surfaces both directions — the inbound
  `context_id` and the context its own calls produce — and the test
  is then an ordinary comparison against a slot the adapter fills.
  Where an adapter does not, v1 offers no way to distinguish the two,
  and the rule has to be shaped so that reacting to its own effect is
  harmless.
